Ready for the maintainer to merge. Safety-tier review (posted G-code). No blockers.

**Where it ran:** locally on macOS, in a trial merge with upstream/main (5c50f6721). No GitHub runner was used.

**What looks good**
- The DIN/ISO sequence is in a safe order: M5, then the M92 retract under the old tool call, then the checks, then M6, then the new T block. No move comes between the retract and the T block.
- The first tool gets the checks and M6 with no retract. A repeated tool number writes no stop.
- The engine law (`manual_change.rs`) refuses by name before any hook runs. It names the post and the machine.
- Machines without a manual mode are not asked, so their output is unchanged.
- The new golden `picomax_two_tools.nc` was checked line by line against the PR body. It matches.
- No other golden or recorded program changed. The decision file is present. Provenance line is present. No `unwrap` outside tests. Files are under 400 lines.

**Results (merged with main)**
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 87 steps ran, 0 failed. The gate then reported VOID ("the checkout moved during the run"), because the trial merge was made while it ran. I did not take it as a verdict. I ran the suites by name instead (below).
- camcraft-post: lib `manual_change` 2 passed; `script_heidenhain` 15; `script_heidenhain_klartext` 23; `machine_controller` 5; `same_angle_arcs` 4; `comment_escape` 4; `same_angle_stream` 4; `coincident_arcs` 4. All passed.
- camcraft-app: `example_catalog` 43 passed (4 ignored, heavy); `example_catalog_adaptive` 1; `example_catalog_edge_work` 1; `conformance` 7; `machine_controller` 3; `klartext_builtin` 33; `deburr_chord_width` 7; `smoothing` 3; `machine` 7. All passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

**Extra suites run:** every test source that names Fehlmann or Picomax (listed above). The diff touches no `testdata/` file and no importer code.

**Mutations (both red, then restored)**
1. Remove the M92 retract block in `heidenhain.cps`: `din_iso_retracts_and_stops_before_the_second_tool_moves` failed.
2. Remove the `manualToolChange` manifest line in `heidenhain.cps`: 3 picomax tests failed (the golden test, the same-tool test, the refusal-table test).

**Heavy lanes:** not run by me. The author reports `app heavy: example_catalog` ok on this head. No other heavy lane is reached by this diff.

**Goldens moved:** none. One new golden is added, and it is listed in the body.

**Not exercised (as the body states):** no run on the real NC 340490-03 control. The `G00 G90 Z+0 M92` block form and the halt at M6 come from the manual and the machine parameters.

**Follow-ups (file after merge, not blocking):** none.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
left for the maintainer: check 6 skip - P1 (safety floor). The review of head 1d70083456 is owed; do not merge in the sweep.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 1d70083456fdee7d07d06df619f376ce9eb07f92 -->
**Second review (P1 safety-floor work): one change is requested before the merge.** @mkinney set `merge-ready` on this head; this comment replaces that label with `needs-rework`, because an open change request wins (AGENTS.md, #3382).

A read-only Opus agent of the coordinator of NeoTech read the diff of head `1d7008345` and issue #4085. It did not read the first review before it formed its view. It built nothing and ran no test.

## What is correct

- The posted program for the shipped Picomax file is correct: `M9` and `M5` at the section end, the retract, the stop, then the T block, `M3` and the coolant from the section preamble. The first tool, the last tool, a repeated tool number, and a tool change with no motion are handled.
- A machine with an automatic changer gets no stop (early return, `heidenhain.cps:387`). Each other post is unchanged by construction (`engine.rs:131-134`).
- `manual_change.rs` has no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!`. The golden agrees with the code. The provenance comment is there.

## Requested before merge

1. **Class: a safety argument that holds for one installation is applied to each installation.** `assets/posts/heidenhain.cps:385-394` (`manualChange`) writes `G00 G90 Z+0 M92` and then `M6` for each machine whose `tooling.tool_change` is `manual-retract-top`. It does not read `machine.controllerIdentity`.
   - "The retract goes only up" depends on the Picomax machine parameters MP 950.2 and MP 4210.0.
   - "`M6` halts the program" depends on MP 7440 bit 0 = 0.
   - `assets/machines/AGENTS.md:306-309` defines `manual-retract-top` as a general value and says that a post must verify whether its procedure serves the installation. The Klartext post does this: it refuses each controller except iTNC 530 / 340490-03 (`heidenhain-klartext.cps:73-75`), stops with `M0`, and retracts with `M140 MB MAX`.
   - Failing case: a user writes a machine file for a different TNC knee mill with `"tool_change": "manual-retract-top"`. If the M92 datum is not at the top, `Z+0 M92` is a rapid in Z with the old tool above the part, before a stop. If MP 7440 bit 0 = 1, `M6` does not halt: `M3` starts the spindle with the old tool, and the length of the new tool is active. That is the defect of #4085 again, and the program posts with no warning.
   - One rule that closes the class: the DIN/ISO post refuses by name each `manual-retract-top` machine whose controller identity is not the one that the procedure was verified for (the same check as the Klartext post). Add the test: a `manual-retract-top` machine with no identity, or with a different identity, is refused. Consider `M0` with or after `M6`, so that the halt does not depend on a machine parameter.

## Notes, not blockers

- `heidenhain.cps:415-417` writes `M6` before the T block. The PR lists the PLC reaction under "Not exercised".
- `manual_change.rs:19`: each shipped post now refuses a user machine that states plain `manual`. This is safe and named. The changelog row covers it only in part.
- `heidenhain-klartext.cps:18`: `manualToolChange` shares a line with `workOffsetMax` to keep the line numbers of the refusal goldens. It works, but it is fragile.
- The decision file says "in both cases the move goes only up". That is true only with the Picomax parameters.

## Not checked

- No build and no test ran. The reviewer relied on the gate that the PR reports.
- If `G00 G90 Z+0 M92` is a legal DIN/ISO block on NC 340490-03.
- How the iTNC applies the tool length to an M92 move.

A fix on the same branch gets a fresh review of the new head.

Reply to the second review (comment 7183504707, head `1d7008345`). Commits `628f8607d` and `6ad78aafd` fix the blocking finding. The new head is `6ad78aafd`. It waits for a fresh review. The PR stays ready (#3727).

## The class rule

The DIN/ISO post now refuses by name each `manual-retract-top` machine that is not the verified installation. The check is in `heidenhain.cps` (`manualInstallation`, called first in `onOpen`). It is the same check as the Klartext post. The machine must have:

- controller identity `iTNC 530` / `340490-03`;
- machine model `Fehlmann Picomax 55 (iTNC 530)`.

The model check is stricter than the review asked. The M92 Z datum and the M06 halt are machine parameters of one installation. A second machine with the same NC software can have different values.

A refused machine stops the post with a script error. Nothing is written. The text:

`Heidenhain TNC: the manual-retract-top tool change (M92 retract, M6, M0 stop) is verified only on the Fehlmann Picomax 55 (iTNC 530) with iTNC 530 NC 340490-03; the machine <model> states <identity, or "no controller identity"> - choose a post that is verified for this installation`

`assets/posts/AGENTS.md` now says that a script that lists a manual mode must also refuse each installation that its sequence was not verified for.

## The tests

`din_iso_refuses_a_manual_change_machine_it_was_not_verified_for` (new, in `crates/post/tests/script_heidenhain.rs`, module `picomax`). It changes the Picomax file in four ways. The post refuses each one by name:

- no controller identity;
- other NC software (`340490-05`);
- another control model (`TNC 426`);
- another machine model.

The test failed on the post of head `1d7008345`. The Picomax still posts: `din_iso_retracts_and_stops_before_the_second_tool_moves` compares the golden and asserts `M5` < retract < `M6` < `M0` < new T block.

## The M0 decision: taken

`M0` now follows `M6` at each change. The reasons:

- With `M6` alone, the halt depends on MP 7440 bit 0. A service change of that parameter does not change the machine file or the identity. Thus the identity check cannot see that change. `M0` halts whatever the parameter says.
- On the Picomax, `M0` also switches the drives off (manual p. 1-17). The operator installs the tool at this stop.
- The Klartext post stops with `M0` at the same point.
- `M6` stays before the checks, because the machine's manual writes it for the change.

The golden `picomax_two_tools.nc` changes: one `M0` block after the checks at each change. The block numbers after the first `M0` move by 10, and after the second `M0` by 20. The program can now halt two times at a change. The decision file records this cost and the dropped orders (`M0` alone, `M0` before `M6`).

## The notes

- Decision file: the sentence "in both cases the move goes only up" now says that this is true with the verified installation's parameters (MP 950.2, MP 4210.0, MP 7440 bit 0). On a different installation the post refuses.
- Changelog row: it now also covers the refusal of each shipped post on a machine that states plain `manual`.
- The Klartext manifest line stays on the `workOffsetMax` line. The PR body says that a later change to the Klartext header must keep the line count or regenerate the refusal goldens.

## Gate on head `6ad78aafd`

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 310 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. This includes `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work`.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The targeted heavy step `cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main --only "app heavy: example_catalog"`: ok.

Ready for a re-check.

Reviewer: MacBook-Pro.local pool job review-4114 (config .claude-team-skull), claude-opus-5-5 (Opus 5.5), login mkinney; did not write or refresh this PR.

**Re-review of the new head `6ad78aafd`: ready for the maintainer to merge.** This is a safety-tier review: the PR changes posted G-code. No blockers.

**Where it ran:** locally on macOS. The trial merge of the PR head with upstream/main `6f31829a8` had no conflicts (merge `bc2118b29`, parent 1 = `6ad78aafd`). No GitHub runner was used.

## Earlier findings (NeoTech review of head `1d7008345`)

1. **Requested: the DIN/ISO post applied the Picomax safety argument to each `manual-retract-top` machine.** Fixed in `628f8607d`.
   - `heidenhain.cps` `manualInstallation()` is the first call in `onOpen`. It refuses each `manual-retract-top` machine without the identity `iTNC 530` / `340490-03` and the model `Fehlmann Picomax 55 (iTNC 530)`. This is the same check as `heidenhain-klartext.cps:73-79`.
   - The refusal is a script error, and nothing is written.
   - The requested test is `din_iso_refuses_a_manual_change_machine_it_was_not_verified_for`. It covers four cases: no identity, other NC software, other control model, other machine model. It passes here. With the call removed (mutation 1, below), it fails.
   - "Consider `M0` with or after `M6`": taken. `M0` follows the checks after `M6` at each change. The golden and the structural assert pin the order `M5` < retract < `M6` < `M0` < new T block.
2. **Note: the decision file said "in both cases the move goes only up".** Fixed. The sentence now limits this to the verified installation's parameters.
3. **Note: the changelog covered the plain `manual` refusal only in part.** Fixed. The `Changelog:` line now names it.
4. **Note: the `manualToolChange` line shares a line with `workOffsetMax` in Klartext.** No change, by the author's choice. The PR body records the constraint. This is not a blocker.

## What I checked in the code

- Each motion block in `heidenhain.cps` states its own G word (`motion()`). Thus the `G00 G90 Z+0 M92` retract cannot leave a modal G00 for the next section. The first move after the T block states `G00 G40 G90` again.
- The retract runs after `M5` (and `M9`) of the section end, and before the new T block. No move comes between the retract and the T block.
- `machine.toolChangeMode` and `machine.model` reach the script through the same mirror as the Klartext post (`machine_installation.rs:42-44, 67-69`; `post/machine.rs:354-357`).
- `manual_change.rs` has no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` outside tests. It has a provenance line. It is 89 lines.
- Main brought in a new wire post (`sodick-ln2w.cps`) and a new machine (`sodick-aq600l.mch`). The machine states no `tooling.tool_change`. `every_shipped_post_without_the_manual_change_is_refused_on_the_picomax` reads `assets/posts/`, so it also covers the new post. It passes on the merge.

## Results (merged with main, locally)

- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: 143 test binaries, 1305 passed, 0 failed (lib, all integration suites, doc-tests). This includes:
  - lib `post::manual_change::tests`: 2 passed;
  - `script_heidenhain`: 16 passed, the 5 `picomax::*` tests included;
  - `script_heidenhain_klartext`: 23 passed;
  - `machine_controller`: 5 passed.
- camcraft-app:
  - `example_catalog`: 43 passed, 4 ignored (heavy);
  - `example_catalog_adaptive`: 1 passed;
  - `example_catalog_edge_work`: 1 passed;
  - `conformance`: 7 passed;
  - `klartext_builtin`: 3 passed;
  - `machine_controller`: 3 passed;
  - `deburr_chord_width`: 7 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- I did not run the full 314-step quick plan. The author reports 310 steps, 0 failed, on this head. The post changes are inactive on each machine that does not state a manual tool change: `manual_change::refusal` returns `None` first, and `manualChange()` / `manualInstallation()` return first.

**Extra suites run:** the Picomax and Fehlmann suites listed above (`deburr_chord_width`, both `machine_controller` suites, `klartext_builtin`) and the catalog suites. The diff touches no `testdata/` file and no importer code.

## Mutations (each red, then restored; the tree is clean)

1. Remove the `manualInstallation();` call in `heidenhain.cps` `onOpen`. Result: `din_iso_refuses_a_manual_change_machine_it_was_not_verified_for` FAILED ("no identity:" with an empty error, so the post wrote a program). The other 4 picomax tests passed.
2. Remove `block(["M0"]);` in `manualChange()`. Result: `din_iso_retracts_and_stops_before_the_second_tool_moves` FAILED on the golden compare (no `M0` after either set of checks).

## Goldens

- I checked the new golden `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/heidenhain/picomax_two_tools.nc` line by line. The sequence is: first tool `M6`, checks, `M0`, T2; at the second tool `M5`, `G00 G90 Z+0 M92`, `M6`, checks, `M0`, T3. The first move with each tool is `G00 G40 G90 Z+10`. It agrees with the code and with the PR body.
- Goldens moved: none. No other `*.nc`, `*.cl` or `examples/catalog/**` file changed.

## Heavy and light lanes

I did not run them. They are not a merge condition. The author reports these results on this head:
- the targeted heavy step `app heavy: example_catalog`: ok;
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed.

## Not exercised (as the body states)

- There was no run on the real NC 340490-03 control.
- The PLC reaction to `M6` before the new T block is not known. The `M0` stop holds in both cases.

## Optional, non-blocking

- `assets/posts/heidenhain.cps:268`: `var nm =(typeof ...`. The space after `=` is missing. This is a style point only.

The NeoTech change request was on head `1d7008345`. This clean review is of the new head `6ad78aafd`, so the request ends here (AGENTS.md "Only collaborators' reviews count"). The author is qsmits. A collaborator merges through `/merge-ready`.
